text:
Avery (CEO): Quick weekly update — clarity on launches, metrics, and immediate asks. TL;DR: EU Dedicated beta roll is scheduled, Private on‑prem pilot with Acme still needs final gating, and we need a brief cost containment plan. Key metrics: p95 latency (text gen) ~180ms, success rate 99.95%, infra spend +6% M/M. Please read and action below.

Avery (CEO): 1) Launch: EU Dedicated canary is green on small traffic but we still need fallback routing for a specific model mismatch (gpt-med-rev). Target: canary -> staged by EOD Wed; full rollout Thu if no regressions.
Avery (CEO): 2) Private pilot: Product + Legal to finalize contract and SOC2 attestation checkpoint. We cannot start onboarding until gating checklist is signed off.
Avery (CEO): 3) Cost: Ops + Finance — propose a temporary smart-throttle cap for best-effort non-prod jobs to hit a 10% runway improvement target.

Priya (VP Product): Noted. I'll publish the Private-pilot gating doc by EOD. Link to draft (internal): https://redwood.internal/docs/private-pilot/gating — will add acceptance criteria for telemetry, rollback, and data path isolation.
Priya (VP Product): Also adding a pre-launch eval: 10 production prompts to validate hallucination/regression risk. Need Eng help to lock prompt set.

Marco (VP Eng): Quick infra note — after the runtime patch we rolled out Friday, we've seen a small p95 regression for gpt-med-2 when context >4k. Rolling patch back in canary tonight and re-run perf harness. If rollback stabilizes, we'll gate the optimizer until further validation.
Marco (VP Eng): For EU canary: deploying canary nodes with reduced batch targets and KV cache enabled. Will add a temporary routing rule to prefer US fallback for customers with strict latency SLAs.

Lin (Head of Reliability): Incident recap: Friday 21:30 UTC — us-west disk pressure caused transient IO wait and a few timed-out requests. Root cause: log rotation process + delayed GC on reclaimed instances. Mitigation: tuned rotation window and added a safety eviction earlier. No customer-visible errors per SLOs, but we saw elevated retry rates for 8 minutes. Runbook updated.
Lin (Head of Reliability): I'll put the updated runbook in the runbooks repo and add a PagerDuty suppression for non-retry-safe backlog spikes during rotation windows.

deploy-bot: deploy started — service: redwood-dedicated/eu canary v1.2.4 by Marco — status: running

Allison (Head of Sales): For the Acme pilot, Sales/legal need: NDA, SOC2 evidence, and a simple SLO appendix. We're not comfortable starting onboarding without SOC2 or an explicit security attestation. Legal is ready to fast-track the NDA.

Ken (Finance): Notes on spend: the +6% M/M is partly demand-driven and partly from larger batch sizes in trials. We can cover runway impact through Q2 if we implement a temporary budget cap on non-customer-scope experiments. I'll send a proposed cap this afternoon.
Ken (Finance): Also: reminder that Dedicated reserved commitments can reduce unit cost; propose a fast-path econ analysis for the top 3 pilot customers.

Avery (CEO): Action items recap: Eng — stabilize canary and rollback if needed; Product — publish gating doc and prompt eval; Reliability — confirm runbook and suppression settings; Sales/Legal — finalize NDA + SOC2 ask; Finance — cap proposal and econ analysis.

Priya (VP Product): I'll schedule a 30m sync for Wed 9:00 PT to review gating checklist and rollout decision.
Marco (VP Eng): I'll post canary metrics to the #engineering-status dashboard and ping when rollback is complete.
Lin (Head of Reliability): Rolling the runbook change now; will follow up with a short postmortem for Friday's spike.
Allison (Head of Sales): Looping Legal now.
Ken (Finance): Sending cap proposal in 30m.

Avery (CEO): Thanks team. If you see anything blocking the canary or pilot, flag it immediately in #incident-response and ping me. Meeting: Monday 10am PT optional sync for execs.

Priya (VP Product): +1
Marco (VP Eng): ack
Lin (Head of Reliability): ack
Allison (Head of Sales): :thumbsup:
Ken (Finance): ack
deploy-bot: deploy status update — canary v1.2.4 health: 4/5 green, 1 slow node under investigation
